children: Elevance Health emerged as the highest-rated national health insurer in UBS’s annual survey of employee-benefit managers, while the three largest pharmacy-benefit managers appear well positioned to withstand a surge in contract reviews for 2027.

UBS analysts led by A.J. Rice surveyed 166 benefits managers at companies with more than 100 employees. The research covered insurers’ competitive standing, expected medical and prescription-drug costs, benefit priorities and purchasing plans for next year.
Elevance
, which operates Blue Cross Blue Shield plans in 14 states, received the highest overall score at 4.34 out of five. UnitedHealth Group
ranked second at 4.23, followed by Kaiser Permanente at 4.20.
Elevance
led the customer-service and provider-network categories. CVS Health’s
Aetna unit received the highest score for care and condition management, while Kaiser placed first for plan support and digital tools.
Cigna
, last year’s overall leader, slipped slightly in the aggregate rankings. However, it retained the top position among employers with 501 to 5,000 workers.

The survey provides encouraging signals for Elevance and UnitedHealth as employers prepare to reconsider an unusually large number of health-plan contracts. Elevance’s first-place ranking could help it compete for new business, while UnitedHealth combines improving customer perceptions with the lowest exposure to clients seeking new bids.

CVS Health and Cigna face more pressure on their insurance books, but their pharmacy-benefit businesses remain competitively strong. At the industry level, accelerating medical costs may support premium increases while also creating risks if insurers misprice plans or fail to control claims.
More employers put contracts up for bid

About 77% of respondents said they planned to seek new proposals for all or a significant portion of their core medical benefits for 2027. That compares with 53% in last year’s survey and 41% a year earlier.
Aetna and Blue Cross Blue Shield plans outside Elevance had the greatest exposure to rebidding, at 90%, followed by Cigna and Elevance. UnitedHealth had the lowest exposure among the major carriers.

The purchasing criteria also shifted. Cost and discounts remained the leading consideration, but only 36% of respondents ranked them first, down sharply from 89% last year. Network breadth ranked second, followed by customer service and care management. Virtual care and flexibility became more important in the selection process.
Medical costs accelerate

Employers expect gross medical costs for self-insured plans to rise 7.9% in 2027, accelerating from an estimated 7% this year. Changes to benefit designs, sometimes known as benefit “buydowns,” are projected to reduce the increase by about 0.3 percentage point, leaving a net cost trend of approximately 7.5%.

Workers at self-insured employers are expected to contribute 5.8% more toward premiums and out-of-pocket expenses next year. Fully insured employers expect employee premiums to increase an average of 5.5%, down from the 8.3% increase projected in the previous survey.

GLP-1 obesity treatments were identified as the biggest contributor to medical-cost growth, followed by higher prices for healthcare services. Specialty medicines and patients with exceptionally expensive conditions also remained significant cost pressures.
Big PBMs retain their advantage

Competition among pharmacy-benefit managers is intensifying, with 92% of respondents reporting that their PBM contracts are due for renewal in 2027. About 65% plan to issue requests for proposals, more than double the 30% recorded last year.

Despite that activity, the three dominant PBMs maintained a favorable competitive position. CVS Caremark, Cigna’s Express Scripts and UnitedHealth’s Optum Rx had relatively low exposure to competitive bidding and were the three most frequently cited as likely to improve their market positions in 2027.

Cost management remained the most important factor in choosing a PBM. Transparency rose to second place alongside specialty-drug management, while the importance of rebates fell sharply. Only 11% selected rebates as a leading consideration, down from 37% last year.
Employers expect prescription-drug costs to rise 5.6% in 2027, compared with an estimated 5.4% this year.
GLP-1 coverage expands sharply

The survey found that 91% of employers now cover newer obesity medicines, up from 52% last year. Most place restrictions on coverage, including prior authorization requirements and minimum body-mass-index thresholds.
UBS estimated that 19.1% of covered workers and dependents use GLP-1 medicines for obesity. Respondents expect that figure to rise to 20.6% next year.

Weight management and mental healthcare are emerging as the biggest areas for additional benefit spending. About 55% of employers expect to increase budgets in both categories, reflecting the growing financial and clinical significance of obesity treatments and behavioral-health services.

title: Elevance leads UBS health benefits survey as employers brace for higher costs
